name: gooey-text
title: Gooey Text
description: Words that melt into each other: two blurred copies cross-fade and an SVG threshold filter merges their edges into one gooey shape.
label: Gooey Text Morphing (21st.dev)
author: Victor Welander <https://21st.dev/@victorwelander>

props.name: texts
props.description: The words or phrases to morph through, in order, looping. The same words in a new array do not restart the morph.

props.name: cooldownTime
props.description: Seconds a word holds before the next morph.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the root. It has no height of its own (the words are absolutely positioned), so give it or its parent a height, as the demo does.

props.name: textClassName
props.description: Classes for both text copies: size, weight and color (upstream: text-6xl, text-[60pt] from md up, text-foreground).

props.name: label
props.description: What screen readers read instead of the moving words. Default: every word, comma separated.

props.name: paused
props.description: Stop the morph where it is, for example behind a pause control.

props.name: renderFirstWordOnServer
props.description: Put the first word in the server render, so the server HTML, a no-JavaScript visit and the first frame show a word instead of nothing. Off by default, as upstream: the text appears with the first morph.

a11y: The morphing copies are aria-hidden. Screen readers read every word once, from a visually hidden span (or the label prop); the moving words are never announced, so nothing interrupts.
Reduced motion: the words swap at the same rhythm with no blur and no fade.
The words change on their own without end. Pair it with a pause control that sets paused when it sits in the reading flow.
The loop pauses off screen, in a hidden tab, in a paused gallery tile and while paused is set, and resumes where it stopped.
